subject.title: [优化建议] install.sh 模块化拆分以提升可维护性

question: Should OpenClaw keep `scripts/install.sh` as a single served shell script for now, or sponsor an owner-approved modular installer architecture that still publishes a safe single entrypoint?
rationale: The request is not a broken current behavior; it changes the structure of a public setup surface whose docs, website sync, tests, and release validation currently assume one script.

options.title: Sponsor a guarded split
options.body: Approve an incremental module layout only if the public installer remains a single safe entrypoint and the website sync plus installer smoke matrix are updated in the same plan.

options.title: Keep focused refactors only
options.body: Leave this issue as a backlog note and continue extracting or deleting small sections only when tied to concrete installer bugs or validation improvements.

options.title: Close as not planned
options.body: Decide that the public shell installer should remain monolithic to reduce packaging and `curl | bash` helper-loading risk.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a guarded split
recommendation.body: Approve an incremental module layout only if the public installer remains a single safe entrypoint and the website sync plus installer smoke matrix are updated in the same plan.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent installer-specific commits and refactor work make Vincent Koc the best available owner for deciding whether the split shape is worth the compatibility cost.
